headline: High: nullclaw can write broad workspace state and egress data while opik has only a REST surface, creating default risks of leakage, conflict, and cascading misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write filesystem, use MCP, and run browsers; opik exposes a REST API. A plausible bridge exists if nullclaw ingests opik-returned content or shared workspace files as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF nullclaw reads opik REST responses from a shared workspace file or MCP channel as instructions, injection is possible.
IF opik returns attacker-controlled text that nullclaw later parses as commands, prompt injection can occur.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on any opik-fed text.
Separate opik outputs from nullclaw prompt inputs.
Require explicit human review before acting on REST payloads.
Use a provenance tag for all cross-agent content.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, conversation history, and workspace files, while opik has broad network egress and a REST API. If they share a workspace or account context, sensitive data can flow from nullclaw into opik outputs or telemetry. The profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF nullclaw and opik share a workspace, logs, or account context, sensitive data can be exposed.
IF opik forwards received content to a third-party backend or telemetry endpoint, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and credentials.
Redact secrets before passing data between agents.
Turn off verbose logging for shared runs.
Review outbound destinations for opik.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; opik has a REST API and broad egress. If both operate on the same mutable resources, overlapping writes or concurrent state changes can conflict. No locking or coordination is documented, so the interaction is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write the same directory or git repository, state conflicts can occur.
IF both agents mutate the same remote resource through REST or network calls, last-write-wins errors can occur.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories or repos.
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock.
Run one agent read-only during the other's write phase.
Snapshot state before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking or transactional updates.

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate and act on workspace content, and opik exposes a REST API that may consume or display that content. If opik treats nullclaw output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF opik ingests nullclaw-produced text without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF either agent triggers downstream actions from the other's output, the error can cascade.
mitigations: Require a human check before downstream actions.
Add schema validation to exchanged payloads.
Mark nullclaw outputs as untrusted by default.
Limit opik to read-only evaluation of nullclaw artifacts.
requires-engineering: implement verification and rollback gates.

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles audit logs, conversation history, workspace files, and secrets, while opik's profile shows no sensitive data classes or special compliance claims. A compliance mismatch is possible only if regulated data is routed into nullclaw and then into opik; the profiles do not show that by default, so low fits. The other agent is cited to show the receiving surface is generic.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through nullclaw into opik logs or exports, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared data class, the pair may violate policy.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair.
Set short log retention on both systems.
Review export and deletion workflows.
Document the data classes allowed in each agent.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls.
